attributes.body_ja:
「という」は、格助詞（かくじょし）の「と」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「言（い）う」からできた表現（ひょうげん）です。たいていはひらがなで書（か）かれます。「という」は、「(A) という (B)」の形（かたち）で二（ふた）つの名詞（めいし）をつなぎます。そして、「(A) と呼（よ）ばれる (B)」や「(A) の名前（なまえ）で知ら（し）れている (B)」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「という」（や動詞（どうし）の「言（い）う」自体（じたい））は、ただ見（み）ただけではわからない情報（じょうほう）を伝（つた）えるときに使（つか）います。例（たと）えば、ある人（ひと）を見（み）たとき、その人（ひと）の名前（なまえ）や仕事（しごと）はわかりません。しかし、身長（しんちょう）や体型（たいけい）などはわかります。「という」は、名前（なまえ）や仕事（しごと）などの情報（じょうほう）を伝（つた）えるときに使（つか）われます。

「(A) という (B)」の形（かたち）が、明（あき）らかな物事（ものごと）に使（つか）われているように見（み）える場合（ばあい）もあります。しかし、その場合（ばあい）、話（はな）し手（て）が「(A) はそうだとは言（い）われてるけど、実（じつ）はちょっと違（ちが）う」とか「(A) が見（み）たままだとは思（おも）わない」などと言（い）いたい場合（ばあい）が多（おお）いです。

このような「という」の使（つか）い方（かた）は、名詞（めいし）だけでなく、いろいろな品詞（ひんし）で見（み）られます。
attributes.body:
という is a combination of the case marking particle と, and the う - Verb 言（い）う. It is a set expression that primarily uses only hiragana. という connects two nouns, and means 'the (B) that is called (A)', or 'the (B) known as (A)'.

Fun Fact

という (and the verb 言（い）う itself) is often quite misunderstood, as the closest translation in English is 'to say'. In Japanese, 言（い）う actually refers to the information about something that cannot be discovered by simply 'looking at' it. For example, if you look at a man, you cannot know that his name is Bob, or that he works in an office, but you can know whether he is 'short', 'tall', etc. Due to this, という should only be used to express information that requires intimate knowledge, and not simple observations.

It is possible to see (A) という (B) in sentences where (A) is describing something that seems 'obvious'. However, in these cases, the speaker is usually implying that something about (A) is not exactly as it seems, or that their opinion/knowledge differs.

This particular nuance is not limited to nouns, and may be seen with almost any word type.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both expressions contain the same という, but are used differently. という is used to name or describe something, typically in the form AというB ('a B called A'). In contrast, というのは introduces something as a topic for explanation or comment, e.g. 人生というのは ('This thing we call life') While という is followed by a single noun, というのは is followed by a phrase that elaborates on the topic.

attributes.body: いわゆる and という both convey the idea of something being referred to by a name, but they function differently. いわゆる comes before a noun to mean 'the so-called (A)'. という appears between two nouns in the form AというB ('a B called A'). Because they serve different grammatical roles, they can appear together, e.g. いわゆる外来語というもの ('What is known as a so-called loanword')

attributes.body: ということ turns phrases into nouns and is often used to clarify or restate something, e.g. 日本に行くということ 'the fact that (he) is going to Japan'. という by itself links a phrase or name to a noun, as in ポチという犬 'a dog named Pochi' or 来年日本に行くという学生 'a student who is going to Japan'.

second_relatable.title: という
second_relatable.meaning: Called, Named, Known as, As much as

attributes.body: という is versatile: AというB = 'a (B) called (A)' or to show hearsay, e.g. 面白いという本 'a book said to be interesting'. といわれている is more formal and emphasizes that something is generally said or believed by many people, especially in written or academic contexts.
